newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Nigeria said planning Freetown strike on Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria said planning Freetown strike on Saturday.

text.p: Sierra Leonean politician John Karefa-Smart said on Friday he had learned from coup leaders that Nigeria planned a military strike on Saturday to restore the ousted civilian government of Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
"Instructions have been given emanating from Nigeria that an invasion is to take place tomorrow morning," said Karefa-Smart, who lost the March 1996 presidential election to Kabbah.
The veteran politician, who has been in contact with the military since the coup, told the BBC African service he had a copy of the order.

"I don't like it, as a Sierra Leonean, I don't want to see my country invaded from outside in the interests of anything, I think if there are problems in Sierra Leone they can be solved internally in Sierra Leone and not by force from outside," he said.
Kabbah asked West African leaders for help in restoring his government. Nigeria has flown in reinforcements and is consulting with Ghana and Guinea.
The United States, which flew out 900 foreigners on Friday, said it opposed any use of force in Freetown.
